chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from his father who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not buy from a corrupter (one who mixes/adulterates goods), for there is no blessing in his transaction.'

key_terms.مُحَارَفٍ: One who mixes or adulterates goods, often to increase weight or volume deceptively.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying from someone who adulterates goods?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against purchasing from a 'muharif', a merchant known for adulterating goods to deceive buyers, noting that such transactions lack divine blessing (barakah). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on commercial integrity and the spiritual consequences of deceit in trade, linking economic honesty to spiritual purity.
